claims.claim: USA.gov's Contact Center is presented as the public's general 'front door' for asking any government agency a question, but the vulnerability-disclosure policy names HackerOne/GSA Bug Bounty Program as the only intake and states there is no separate route to move a misrouted report into the program on the reporter's behalf. A member of the public who finds a TTS vulnerability and naturally goes through the front door they were taught to use (USAGov Contact Center) reaches a channel that cannot carry the report anywhere, and the reporter is left with no stated next step other than starting over at HackerOne, which they may not know exists or be willing to use.

The password-requirements page teaches that account recovery must be a deliberately chosen, organization-controlled mechanism (e.g. explicitly naming iCloud as 'your recovery method for forgetting your laptop password'). The Slack offboarding flow breaks this pattern without acknowledging it: converting a leaving partner or contractor to a Single-Channel Guest disables their 2FA and swaps their address to a personal email nobody at the organization administers, so the account's 'forgot password' path now silently exits through a mailbox outside any controlled recovery flow. Nothing in the offboarding procedure flags this as a state requiring a decision, and there is no described fallback if that personal mailbox is later compromised or abandoned.

The IAA process treats collecting the actual authorizing instrument as a mandatory, load-bearing step: an Economy Act Determination must be signed by the requesting agency and assembled into the package before OGC/GSA signature. The IGCA process for state and local partners diverges from that pattern at the equivalent point: when the request letter comes back signed by a designated official rather than the chief executive, the account manager only confirms a delegation or authorizing statute exists but does not collect the instrument itself, and it is explicitly not one of the items assembled into the package that goes to review and signature. Anyone checking the executed IGCA package for proof of signing authority hits a dead end with no artifact to point to and no described way to produce one after the fact.
